chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said, 'A man cuts off the head of a deceased person.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The sanctity of the deceased is like the sanctity of the living.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on the sanctity and dignity of a deceased person?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the legal principle of *hurmat al-mayyit*, equating the sanctity of the deceased with that of the living. It serves as a foundational basis for prohibiting mutilation and disrespect, such as decapitation, extending the rights of the body (*hurmat al-jasad*) beyond death. This ruling underscores the continuity of human dignity in Shia jurisprudence, linking physical integrity to spiritual respect.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Sinan, from the one who informed him, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I said, ‘A man cuts-off the head of a deceased’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The sanctity of the dead is like the sanctity of the living’.
